Voted "Man of the Match" at the Horsham YA Meeting for his 1.78 high jump, James Ganio has made a big impact on the jumps, sprints and shot in our Boy's team.
James Hilston and Gavin Jones also gave us a double victory in the U15 high jump. There was an excellent performance from James Ganio, an U17, who won both the triple and the long jumps.
Above: More great triple jumping came from James Ganio in 1993.

James Ganio was impressive in winning the under-17 long jump and Pam Friel had to settle for a silver medal winning effort in the 200 metres after finding that several of the events were cancelled due to insufficient entries.

A great double win came from high jumpers Mark Arend and James Ganio, and Jamie Webb again did the business in the pole vault but once more the team had a makeshift look about it as we had to get people competing 'just for the point'; when did you last see Guy Sagar and Bob Bridges forming our 800m line-up?
James Ganio had the misfortune to turn his ankle on his very first long jump attempt, while James Hilston's back problem had him unable to compete at all.
Super triple jumping came from James Ganio and James Hilston and Marlon Dickson was looking really hot in the sprints in his first year in the age group.
